Well, I don't want to ruin it for you in case you read it.
No, I won't be reading it, don't worry.
He joined a pop group with three other people, he was brilliant.

We've also got Stephen Poliakoff's The Lost Prince. You can have that in your collection. Probably never watch it, but it might look like you're slightly classy and arty. And uh...

They'll take Ricky back to their planet

(high pitched, amazed) "I'd love that! I'd love-"
--worries me is they might bump into you-WHAT if they bump into you!? What if they bump into you and they think you represent mankind.

ex: Basically, you- they just send your information ahead to the airport and you just drive through a, kind of, drive through McDonald's-style check-in, they take your bag, they take your passport, boom, they drop you off at the executive…
He forget- he forgets the bloke's name but they had- he had lovely--

q: Steve rang Ricky to admit he didn't know passports expired. What was his reasoning?
x: He'd only ever used it once
Nobody had ever checked it before

ex: He called me- he called me, right, he said, "Rick, I've really mucked up-", "Go on.", he went, "My passport expired." I went, "Awww. So what are you gonna do?!" He went- he said, right, I c- he went, "I didn't know passports expired."

I went, "What do you mean?", I went- he went, "Well, your driving license doesn't." I went, "What are you talking about?!" He said, "How old do you have to be to know that?" He said- he said, "When will I know all these things."
(laughing) He went, "When will I know all these things?"

Ah, you're an idiot, play a record.
Ryan Adams - Answering Bell Begins To Play

These are ghosts who walk the st- walk the earth as the undead just winding people up slightly.
A cat that did not look happy.
But seriously why would ghosts wander around just like winding people up?

Rick, i’m worried we’re getting a little bit high brow
Have we got any knob gags you could do? Quikly cos i just think there’s a lot of people who are going to be turning off

Ohhh Careful, Rick, careful. Because you could scold your hands, but what about your elbows?
I wish I knew what that meant. I wish I knew what that meant. I didn't really think that through...

q: Steve got his parents' Volvo estate wedged across a narrow lane, with a stolen pig in the back. What rescue did he picture being needed?

A farmer dragging it out with a tractor
The AA with a tow truck

ex: So they’re having a wild time, hilarious. So this time, now we get to a sort of dead end in the, in the road, and they say “well turn round, let’s go back to the party…” I’m thinking ‘fine’, try and do a three point turn in this very…
Was it loads of blokes with like pitchforks and flaming torches going “burn him; he’s playing with our pig…”

Exactly that, and, and so then, you know, I was so terrified that all I could think was there gonna have to send a helicopter to lower a magnet, onto the top of the car to lift the car up and put it the right way round.
You used to read a lot of comics didn’t ya?

q: On XFM, Steve was distracted and busy making phone calls during the show. What was his problem?

He'd promised Neil Young a live session

I told you Rick, I’ve made promises to people that I can’t keep.
I promised about three different people that I’m getting them tickets. So, uh--
Just making some calls, Rick, that’s all.
I can’t believe it. I cannot believe it.

q: Steve buys two sandwiches at a quid each from Benji's because he needs more food than most people. What did he compare himself to?

He is. We have to go to Benji’s, he gets two sandwichs that have to fill him up, right, ‘cos they’re a quid each.
Well I’m a big guy I need a lot more food. I need, genuinely, a lot more food than most people. I’m like a Brontosaurus.
It is. He’s just grazing all day.
So I’m, look, you know I can’t afford to splash out in Pret A’Monge all the time with your fancy French sandwiches!

Or, we're on a tin pot station that no one listens to, now...

The TV show. I have no idea when you--
That is a winner. "You are John Thomson."

He was mugged by a samba dancer

Oh, God Almigh... Were you like Paul 'The Party Animal' Parker?
He would not have been able to keep up if he was with me.
God, what did you do? What did you get up to?
Let me tell you right now, day one, I almost drowned. Day two, I got a foot infection and spent the day in the hospital. And the rest of time I had diarrhea.
So that's, that's, that was a hell Of a. That was a hell of a time.

Slept with his eyes taped open

…but… but the… but the wallet was still there so how, what do you think of them apples? Eh?

42 inch plasma screen. What'd it cost you three grand or something?
Well don't tell 'em. That, that's delush.
Three and a half. Three and a half grand.
Three and a half grand. Big spender. 'Course it's too big.
Well, I can't get far enough back in my room. In my living room for it.

q: As Steve's TV delivery man left, he held his hand out expecting a tip. What had Steve actually reached into his pocket for?

ex: But the problem was I didn't realize and I was thinking to myself, "I wonder if I've got tip him?" And the guy was leaving, and my mobile phone went off in my pocket.
And I reach in to get it, he put his hand out thinking it was a tip. I went, I went, "It's just my phone."
Then so, I felt terrible after he left. I didn't know, I what, what was I gonna do run down the street and offer him a fiver.
Of course not, I'm not made of money. I just spent it all on a TV.

Should we.. should we go along?

Imagine that, imagine going to suck...

q: Steve said he was "looking forward" to Denis Norden's Laughter File at Christmas. Why did he reckon It'll Be Alright On The Night had been renamed?

So it could be repeated more often

Awww, seven, you're having a laugh! Twenty seven!
It used to be It'll Be Alright On The Night, but I think they changed the name to Dennis Norden's Laughter File to fool us.

And they're getting very very thin.

Santa sharing Roses with his reindeer

q: According to Steve, Cliff Richard's new single mashed up 'Somewhere Over The Rainbow' with which song?

I wasn't really listening, I was looking at the pictures an' that, I couldn't believe...
It's What A Wonderful World, combined with Somewhere Over The Rainbow.
Two classic songs, two songs that have been done definitively by artists in the past, he tried to combine them, with a kind of Yamaha keyboard sound in the background.
What was his last year's one? It was Lord's Prayer with Auld Lang Syne.
He's just obsessed with combining two songs, like they're not good enough as they are, "People'll get bored, we'd better combine them".

q: Steve pitched a feature called 'Something old, something new, something borrowed, something blue'. What would 'something borrowed' be?

No, it's all four, you can play that over the course of the show, or maybe you can play four songs in a row, and that's that section.

q: What did Steve sing, with no piano, from the back of the room at his audition for the Bristol Operatic Society?
f: They looked at him "like I was the weirdest freak they'd ever had", then put him straight in the chorus. That's how desperate they were for blokes.
ex: Yeah. Alright, calm down. And, um, I, uh, I went in and they said, “What are you going to sing?” I went, “Uh, well, I’ll just- I-I want to surprise you.” They said, “Do you want a piano accompaniment?” I said, “No, I don’t think so.”
So, I went to the back, I swear to God, I went to the back of the room and I just sang-

Steve sings “Thumbelina, Thumbelina, tiny little thing/ Thumbelina dance, Thumbelina sing/ Thumbelina, what's the difference if you're very small?/ Coz when your heart is full of love, you're six feet tall!”

I just did that and they just looked at me like I was the weirdest freak they’d ever had. Immediately put me in the chorus cause that’s how desperate they were for blokes. We staged- we rehearsed it, I couldn’t remember the lyrics.

q: Hearing that Karl's mam kept him home in case he got blown into the road, Steve asked if that was why she got fired from where?
f: Steve pictured her ringing in to work: "I'm not coming in today, I might get blown into the road."
ex: Well me- me mam just said, uhh, "You might get blown into the road so don't go in."
She had so much faith in you, didn't she... as a human being?
Is that why she got fired from the pie shop?
"I'm not coming in today, I might get blown into the road."

q: Steve said Karl's toad-in-the-mouth remedy sounded like brilliant medical knowledge, but he had one question. What was it?
a: How could the doctor see past the toad to the tonsils?
x: Where would a doctor get a toad from?
f: "Is it not hopping around in the way?" Karl's answer: "It- it didn't say." He then admitted he'd found it on the internet.
ex: No I- I- sure. My initial thought is, it sounds like a brilliant bit of sort of medical uh- knowledge that, it's a great idea.
My only thought is how does the doctor see past the toad-
Yeah what's he looking at with the mouth open? Surely the toad is in the way.
Is it not hopping around in the way?

q: When Ricky read the 'Track Ending Now' warning out on air, why did Steve tell him off?
a: He was giving away the secrets of radio
x: Karl hadn't cued up the next song
f: Steve said listeners think it's vinyl on a needle, like old footage of Tony Blackburn: "Rick, you're showin' 'em behind the curtain! Never do that."
ex: Nirvana, Man Who Sold the World. Karl’s all confused ‘cause it didn’t tell you it’s ending, did it. What is that, a sort of glitch in the –
Careful they might start swearin’. You know what they’re like.
Yeah, and all their habits and that.
Yeah, it says Track Ending Now.

Stop talkin’ about it! That’s – that’s, you’re givin’ away all the secrets, of radio, an’ that. People think it’s like an old piece of vinyl that we’ve put on a needle, you know, like those old bits of footage of Tony Blackburn. That’s…

q: Karl said germaphobes who won't even shake hands are "going to die of something". What did Steve suggest it would be?
f: Karl's advice: "You can't be that paranoid. Gotta get on with your life". Steve's one-word answer: "Loneliness".
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to Medicine · 2008
ex: Yeah. So, you know, it's always there, colds and flus everywhere. That's interesting, isn't it? That more sort of colds are spread through shaking hands than people, you know, just taking in the air. Because people sneeze into their hand…
Yeah, that's going too far, because they're going to die of something. You can't be that paranoid. Gotta get on with your life

q: Ricky's mum played Jim Reeves; Karl's mum had Dr. Hook on during Sunday dinner. What did Steve say about music in his parents' house?
x: They only ever played Cliff Richard
His dad played brass band records
His mum sang opera while hoovering
f: Steve: "My parents didn't like music. Silence." Karl's mum and dad's house is the opposite: music "in every room, all different", which does Suzanne's head in.
ex: My mum was Jim Reeves. She always. Jim Reeves.
My parents didn't like music. Silence. Oh, no, it was constantly. Never put record on.

Oh, our house. Suzanne does her head in when she comes around to Mum and Dad's house because there's music on in every room, all different. And my mum's got into this fella called Roger Fender or something, some country western singer. And…

q: Steve blamed Zoe Ball for poaching Karl. According to Steve, she can't find her own what to get on the show?
f: Steve: "She can't find her own, you know, gibbon to get on the show... don't start stealing ours."
ex: I blame Ball as well, to be honest.
I feel Ball is slightly responsible for it.
She can't find her own, you know, gibbon to get on the show.
She can't find her own, kind of, you know, loser, then... don't start stealing ours.

q: Karl described the bison on 'The Mammals': a really big hairy head, sort of bald at the back. What did Steve say it sounded like?
a: Someone Karl went to school with
x: A mop left out in the rain
Ricky first thing in the morning
f: Steve: "It sounds like someone you went to school with." Ricky's follow-up: "Was there two of 'em?"
ex: Sort of, bald at the back--
It sounds like someone you went to school with.

q: What was the name of Steve's hip-hop record feature?
f: Ricky reckoned the name proved they could work in advertising: "If there's anyone listening like... Satchi and Satchi... then we are the people."
ex: Yeah, I'm going to be playing a hip-hop track.
It's called, it's called the hip-hop track.
Aww we just, brilliant. If there's anyone listening like, you know, erm Satchi and Satchi, or macanex or whatever, you know those people that do advertising then we are the people.

q: When two blokes at a petrol station asked if he wanted to buy some speakers, why did Steve instantly say "Yes I do!"?
a: He was flattered they thought he was that kind of bloke
x: He thought they were from Xfm
He'd just been paid by the BBC
He thought it was a TV prank
f: They thought he'd "need some kind of classy speakers" and would "buy them on the sly." Ricky: "they've seen I look a bit of a hustler."
ex: Um, we’re talking about embarrassing stories and stuff, and I don’t know if I’ve told this on this radio before, have I told you Karl? I’m not sure. But this was when I was workin’ at the BBC, this is not even long ago, and I’d moved to…
Because, I – I’ll tell you the reason .. it was like I was so flattered, that they thought that I’d be the kind of bloke who would A. need some kind of classy speakers,
And B., would like to buy them on the sly.
I thought, I like the fact that,

q: Steve gave his Vietnamese driver a $20 tip. What did his guidebook say he should have given?
f: Steve then fretted the other drivers would find out: "They're all going to be expecting a big tip."
ex: I hopped in a rickshaw, straight back to the hotel, where they do not laugh at me openly. But anyway, it's just returned to the dong issue, right? This was what worried me was that obviously got a tip. So we had a driver for a few days…

Now, but now I'm but no because A you don't want to upset the pressures equilibrium. You don't upset the financial equilibrium because you might have gone berserk. Yeah, in 20 that's $20 is lots and you might have left his family you know…
So what if he turned up with a hat like yours and said exactly remakes know what we're mates. Now, let's go back to England,
Let's pick up some some lady. So, um, so I

I was a bit worried so, I-I- was thinking of asking for the money, you know, for some change. But I didn't think that was appropriate. So um, but then I was worried because I was thinking, what if all the other drivers within his…

q: Engineers took about 25 minutes to come and fix XFM's broken desk. What was Steve's theory about why?
a: They fixed Capital, Capital Gold and people's car radios first
x: They were all on a tea break in the canteen
They couldn't find XFM's studio in the building
They'd heard Karl had broken it on purpose
f: Steve: "Do you feel like we're maybe quite low in the pecking order in the building?" Ricky: "Definitely."
ex: You noticed how it took, um-
-about 25 minutes for them to come down as well though. Do you feel like we're maybe quite low in the pecking order in the building?
You know it's like Capital first, Capital gold, they can shoot off, do other sort of pirate stations.
Peoples car radios, then they come back here.

q: When Ricky took Steve bowling in Finsbury Park, what did Steve's size 14 bowling shoes look like to Ricky?
f: Ricky: "they're so long and thin... it looked like Krusty's ... Krusty the Clown's feet." Steve: "It is a huge size ... shoe."
ex: So you must have looked like a wall bracket with that. What is that? I went bowling with him once the first time and he and we went bowling in this place. Where was it? Must of been Finsbury Park and, uh, I'd never been before and it is…
Anyway and they're multicolored aren't they? They're two colors and it looked like Krusty's ... Krusty the Clown's feet. And then that it's Steve's going "alright." 14, that is big innit?
It is a huge size ... shoe. You're right.

q: Steve said that if he'd been at dinner with Bowie, he'd be chanting in his head: "Don't mention..." what?
f: Steve: "Don't even bring it up. Don't even say you like it cause you don't know what he feels about it." Ricky confirmed he hadn't mentioned it.
ex: You didn’t, you didn’t mention Tin Machine.
I didn’t mention Tin Machine, no.
Cause I’d just be there just thinking, “Don’t mention Tin Machine, don‘t mention Tin Machine.”
“Don’t even bring it up. Don’t even men- don‘t-don’t even say you like it cause you don‘t know what he feels about it.”

q: Ricky couldn't remember the name of a talk show host who's "not Jerry Springer". Steve guessed Montel Williams, then which R&B singer?
f: Ricky's best clue was "'Bout fifty." Claire cracked it: "Maury!" (Maury Povich).

q: Karl revealed Suzanne had got bored of her Christmas present: condoms. What did Steve imagine she'd been doing with them?
a: Filling them with water and throwing them at passing kids
x: Using them as rubber gloves for the washing up
Making balloon animals for the neighbours
Keeping Karl's sandwiches fresh in his lunchbox
f: Steve's other theory: she'd been "putting them on her head and inflating them." Ricky checked whether Karl meant the condoms "or the food that she ate?"
ex: Or the food that she ate?
(Laughing) Yeah. She- she's got tired of filling them with water and throwing them at passing kids--
Or putting them on her head and inflating them.

q: What was Steve's 'genius' method for the ultimate crime?
a: Shoot them with an arrow made of ice from a room across the street
x: Hit them with a frozen leg of lamb, then cook it
Drop a giant icicle on them from a rooftop
Poison their stamps so they die licking them
f: The arrow "melts, dries out, there's no murder weapon". Karl's verdict: "It's an old one."
ex: Did, did I ever tell you my method Karl, my genius method of, erm, assassinating someone, this is brilliant, this is the ultimate crime.
Is this the ice cube one?
Have I told it to you before?
No, but I know about it.
When you shoot an ice bullet...

q: Ricky had been coughing and wheezing and worried he might be allergic to his cat. What was Steve's solution?
f: "I'm not a trained doctor but that's how I'd sort that one out." After all, Steve said, cats "always land on their feet".
ex: Well the- I- well, it seems that easy, but...
Throw- throw it out the window.
That's how- that's how I'd sort out that!
I'm not- I'm not a trained doctor but that's how I'd sort that one out.

q: On Steve's family coach trip back from Paris, what happened to the family who refused to go into the roadside restaurant?
a: They were locked in the coach
x: They were left at the side of the road
They were charged double for their sandwiches
They were made to dress as Butlins redcoats
f: They'd brought sandwiches and just wanted the port. Steve "looked back and just saw this kid with his face pressed up against the glass."
ex: Yeah, they stitched you up. Well I remember we were on a-it was a family trip to France once, we went to Paris. We got the coach, coming back from Paris to one of the ferries, one of the ports, Calais or wherever it was. Coach trip, that's…
"Take me with you. I want to go in the restaurant". They were just stuck in there, I mean, absolutely livid, as you would be.

q: Jonathan Ross said he'd walked in and found "three old men" at XFM. How did Steve protest about his age?
f: Ross was unmoved: "Yeah. You're wrecked! You all looked wrecked!" Steve's excuse: "That's 'cause we're always partyin'!"
ex: I walked in here, and I came in here, and I thought this is the young happenin’ place, and what do I see in here? Three old men sittin’ --
What are you talkin’ about?! I’m only 28! 27.
Yeah. You’re wrecked! You all looked wrecked!

q: According to Steve, how did his friend think the Elephant Man ended up looking like an elephant?
x: He was bitten by a radioactive elephant
He drank elephant milk as a baby
He slept in the elephant enclosure
f: Steve compared it to Spiderman being bitten by a spider: "The Elephant Man! The power of an elephant!"
ex: Well, my friend, my friend said to me when we- he said, “Watch this.” He said, “What happens is he gets trampled on by some elephants and that’s what makes him look like an elephant.”

And I went, “Right.” I watched it and I thought, “That’s not the case” and I tried to explain it to him and he, to this day, is still convinced that the Elephant Man- It’s like a, it’s like when Spiderman--
It was his mam, wasn’t it.
“The Elephant Man! The power of an elephant!”

q: Steve said that, even at the best of times, Ricky sounds like he's doing what?
f: Steve's put-down came after Ricky called last week's burger-eating show "the most appalling piece of radio I have ever heard in my life."
ex: To be fair, though, at the best of times, you sound like you’re selling The Evening Standard.

q: Karl asked what happens if we ruin Earth and move to another planet. Why did Steve say we couldn't go to Mars?
a: It's full of stuff that used to be in Dixons
x: Karl's already put his name down for it
It hasn't got a decent chippy
f: Steve was building on Karl's theory that Mars is a tip. Ricky agreed: "It's like a tip."
ex: What would happen, right? We ruin this world, right? Goes wrong in that, right. They shut it down, they go, we're moving. We go to another planet.
It's as simple as that in his world. It's as simple as that.
We can't go to Mars because it's full of stuff that used to be in Dixons.
Yeah, it's a nightmare. So we can't go there, we go somewhere else.

q: Since cameras aren't allowed in UK courts, Steve imagined a sketch artist drawing Karl's jury. What did he say the picture would show?
a: Eleven people and a sort of Krusty the Clown figure
x: Eleven people and a Mr Potato Head
Eleven people and a Humpty Dumpty
Eleven people and a Bart Simpson figure
f: Ricky pictured the artist doing everyone in detail "and then just a little round head." Steve's verdict: "Charlie Brown."
ex: I would have loved to see it because in this country you're not allowed to show pictures of jurors. You can't take photos in a courtroom. So there's always these sketch artists that draw drawings and it's on the news. The idea that we'd…
Yeah. I would love to see the artist doing you because it would be like "Complicated people, oh yeah, he looks inter, characterful" and then just a little round head.
Yeah. Charlie Brown sitting on the end!

q: Ricky admitted he'd tried explaining telescopes that see back to the Big Bang to Karl in a cafe. What did Steve ask?
x: "Did you draw it on a napkin?"
f: Steve was aghast: "Why...did you do that?" Ricky, describing Karl's face: "I can see his head bleeding."
ex: I was trying to explain to him yesterday, uh, in a cafe, about, um, telescopes that can see back to the Big Bang, and--

Well, I was trying to explain what a light-year was. Then, I was explaining to him that, you know...you sit down, you - you put your telescope on, you're looking at a star, the star explodes. That star exploded a million years ago, and he…
--that's how long it took to get. ((incoherent stammer)) look at him, look at his face. I - I can see his head bleeding.
I just don't (sighs)...so are you saying--
Why did you start doing this in a cafe, Rick? Was it a 24 hour cafe?

q: After Karl left for Cornwall, Ricky predicted the locals would make him King. Steve compared it to the Ewoks in Return of the Jedi elevating which character because he could speak their language?
f: Ricky reckoned "the mayor is probably an animal" and "the townsfolk think like Karl", so Karl would "stay there and be made King".
ex: Because I think one, the mayor is probably an animal. --
And I imagine the townsfolk think like Karl.
Do you know what I mean? I imagine he’ll probably, he’ll stay there and be made King
Have you ever seen Return of the Jedi?
In Return of the Jedi, the Ewoks, the little furry creaturs, they see C3PEO and because he can talk and he can speak the language they actually elevate him--

q: Asked what you'd say you needed big blocks of ice for, what cover story did Steve happily adopt for his perfect murder?
f: Ricky offered "I'm a sculptor" and Steve loved it: "You don't need a license for that. Like you would with a gun."
ex: Where do you get that from?
Well you can buy big blocks of ice I'd expect.
Yeah. Okay. But no, um, you haven't left a trail of like, no one's followed you home or-
What do you say, what do you say you're using it for? I'm a sculptor.
I'm an ice sculptor. Absolutely. You don't need a license for that. Like you would with a gun.

q: Asked how Steve's looks had improved, Karl praised his hair and his stylish glasses. What advice did he add?
f: Ricky collapsed laughing, and Steve's only comeback was: "Some people like tall men."

q: Steve once watched Footloose in America. How did he describe the film?
a: Like a film about humans made by aliens who'd only watched our TV and films
x: Like a pop video that goes on for two hours
Like a public information film about dancing
Like a school play with a Hollywood budget
f: Ricky summed up the plot as "That famous film about where- where dancing was banned." Steve called it "an extraordinary film."
ex: But who would get Kenny Loggins then? If the- if the clue was good, who would get Kenny Log- What did he do? Footloose?
That famous film about where- where dancing was banned.

That's an extraordinary film. I saw it once in America. Like you say, Kevin Bacon, in a town where dancing has been banned. I was watching it. It was like if aliens had been watching earth but only monitoring us through our tv and films.
And then tried to make a film about humans. That's the film they'd end up with.

q: Karl didn't make his point to jellyfish expert Vicky because it might have confused her. Finish Steve's reply: "Well, she's a scientist..."
f: Karl had held back because raising it "would have took her off and confused her".
ex: No, but the turtle thing, you know, if you get rid of 'em then the turtles, you know, won't have anything to eat... But, when she said that, I mean, I couldn't say it cuz it would have took her off and confused her but, like--
Well, she's a scientist, she's easily confused.

q: For listeners who've never seen Karl, Steve said he looks a bit like which children's TV character?
f: Ricky agreed straight away ("He does! He does!") and added that Karl is the missing link: "half human, half monkey."
ex: Yeah. Well for those that have never seen Karl, I actually, if you remember, I think he looks a little bit like Mr. Spoon from Button Moon.
If you've ever seen that show--

And also he looks like, you know when they say they find a little four-foot human and it's actually half a million years old and they give it a name. It's the first you know, Australopithecus into, right? He looks like one of them as well.
Perfectly round little, he's the missing link. He looks half human, half monkey.

q: Ricky described sitting by the fire after dinner with a cigar and a nice Pinot Grigio. What did Steve ask him?
f: Steve already thought the golf trip sounded romantic. When Ricky mentioned the meal, he asked: "Candlelit?"
ex: That's it. But anyway, so we have our meal, which is really nice.
Then we're sitting in the bar, I'm having a cigar by the fire. But we're having a rather nice Pinot Grigio. He's there go--
Is this 1955 that you live in?

q: A homeless man told Steve: 'I'm from Liverpool and I'm homeless.' What did grumpy Steve want to say back?
f: Steve: "Go back to Liverpool. That's why you're homeless, you're in London!" Later: "He could have just said, 'I'm from Liverpool' - I'd have given him some change."
ex: Just got off the train and em... guy comes up to me and he says 'Excuse me, can you spare some change? I'm from Liverpool and I'm homeless'.
And I was so angry. I-really-I was in a bad mood anyway and I just wanted to say to him 'Well, there's your mistake.'
Go back to Liverpool. That's why you're homeless, your in London!

q: At a festival in Steve's home town of Bristol, Robert Plant bored the crowd with old blues covers until he played which song?
f: Steve's crowd reaction: "Wahay! You should've done all the old Led Zeppelin. Stop playing all this other nonsense we're not interested in!"
ex: And I was at a little - they have a little kind of music festival back in my home town of Bristol, periodically in the summer. They can never really attract any decent acts, but you know, we support them anyway.

I think, well this year it was Robert Plant - uh, who sang lots of Old Blues covers and people were quite bored until he played Whole Lotta Love at the end and then we sort of went "Wahay! You should've done all the old Led Zeppelin. Stop…

q: Steve ran into a married friend he'd known for years. What phrase did the friend use that made Steve want to shout "Use her name!"?
f: The friend said: "Oh, the wife will be along in a minute." Steve: "I know who she is, I know her name."
ex: Yeah I remember bumping into someone, friends of mine, somewhere at a party, to a couple I knew, and I knew both of them before they got married. In fact, I’d known her, I think, longer. And I said “where’s so and so” and he went “Oh, the…
(laughing) I know, I know who she is--
I know who she is, I know her name--
What, I used to call her by that--

q: Designers keep asking whether they can dress Ricky for the Emmys. What did Steve suggest the Emmy committee really meant?
a: Can someone make sure he actually turns up dressed?
x: Can someone keep him away from the buffet?
Can someone make him look a bit taller?
Can someone stop him laughing during speeches?
f: Karl's only question was "Do they do pajamas?" Ricky went further: "Can we tuck him in and leave his slippers at the hotel."
ex: I look good in anything, mate. That's the. That's the difference now. Doesn't matter. Armani could dress me. Doesn't matter. Yeah, he's not. I mean, not that he'd want to. I can't believe I keep getting offered from people like him. And…

Well, exactly one, I think. Why do they want to. What is that going to put sales up? Is someone going to be watching that? And go, yeah, that bloke looks short and fat and sweaty. Get me Armani on the phone.
Maybe that's someone from the Emmy committee going, can you phone up Ricky Gervais and just check that when they say, can we dress him from the Emmys, we mean, can we make sure he's dressed?

Yeah. Can we tuck him in and leave his slippers at the hotel. But, yeah, so I don't do it anyway because I'm mildly embarrassed. We went around those sort of luxury lounges where they give you things. They give you these, like suits, like…

q: Steve finally hit back at Karl's comments about his looks. What did he say Karl looks like?
a: A party balloon with a face drawn on, inflated halfway
x: A boiled egg wearing a parka
A thumb with a face drawn on
A peeled potato in a hat
f: Steve: "You know seriously, can I be honest with you?... Just a little balloon, like a party balloon." Karl's only reply: "Right."
ex: Whenever we get on this conversation, I always think to myself, ‘Karl, do you know what you look like?’

You know seriously, can I be honest with you? You look like- you know if you got like a balloon, a hot air balloon right? Just a little balloon, like a party balloon. If you drew a little face on it, right? And inflated it about halfway…
Ricky laughs and struggles to speak
So. Play a record I don’t wanna get into this. It’s too intense.

q: Steve said he was "furious" after returning an old lady's lost purse. Why?
a: She only sent a little thank-you note, with no cash
x: She accused him of taking money out of it
She sent him a postcard of her cat
She said it wasn't even her purse
f: Steve: "I could have kept that purse I sent it back to you I need more than a little thank you note."
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to The English · 2009
ex: No it was like when I found that old lady's person I sent it back to her and she sent me a little thank you note with nothing, no cash, nothing - I was furious I thought. Come on. I could have kept that purse I sent it back to you I need…

q: Steve moaned that you never see boxers with glasses. Who did he name as his one bespectacled athletic role model?
f: Steve: "So I got no kind of athletic role models in that way, except Dennis Taylor." He added: "I could write a book on the difficulties of having glasses."
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to The English · 2009
ex: Exactly. This is the problem, isn't it? People don't think that you'd never see boxers with glasses.
Right, exactly. So I got no kind of athletic role models in that way, except Dennis Taylor.
(laughing) Oh god. A man with glasses. Me and my classes.
I'll tell you this. I could write a book on the difficulties of having glasses.

q: As a boy, Steve learned a rude word at school, thinking it was just a stronger 'twit'. What happened when he used it at home?
a: His dad didn't know what it meant either and started calling Steve's mum it
x: His mum washed his mouth out with soap
His dad grounded him until Christmas
His nan started saying it at bingo
f: Steve: "my dad didn't know what it meant either… So he started using it as well!" He's never told him, and wonders whether to this Christmas.
ex: And, uhm… and so I started using this at home ‘cause I didn’t realize what it meant. I started using this at home, “Oh, you twit, you’re a twit,” and saying it to my dad, “You’re a twit, you’re a t—,” you know… but not saying “twit.”
And my dad didn’t know what it meant either.
Which I couldn’t believe. So he started using it as well! Right? So then we’ll be driving in the car, he’d be saying to my mum, “You stupid twit…”

q: Looking back on 2005, Steve said the only time he'd prayed for a natural disaster of Biblical proportions was while watching what?
f: "And it never happened." Ricky added that the only big wind on the island came from Rebecca Loos.
ex: It's been terrible. Well, we've had the, obviously Hurricane Katrina and the tsunami and the earthquake and things, and, um, and it's obviously been terrible and we don't want to be, to be flippant about that. But the only time I was…

And it, and it never happened. And some of the dregs of humanity on that show. I mean I don't know if you saw it, but Paul Danan is a joy because he's a mental case. And I'm saying that, I don't know if that's libelous but, I mean, if…

q: When Ricky assured listeners that Karl means no harm and 'knows not what he says', who did Steve compare Karl to?
f: Ricky howled with laughter, then insisted Karl "hasn't got a prejudicial bone in his body".
ex: Can I just say anyone who's offended by this, he means no harm. He doesn't. He knows not what he says, really everything from Karl is totally genuine. He's not having a go. You Live and Let Live, don't you? There is a...
He's a bit, he's a bit like Mork from Mork and Mindy.
He hasn't got a prejudicial bone in his body, but go on then.

q: Ricky called Radio 2's presenters 'dregs'. Steve insisted they're top-calibre broadcasters, but how did he end up describing them?
x: Blokes who used to read the traffic
Anyone who owns an ELO album
f: Asked to name one of these top-calibre broadcasters, Steve said: "I can't name them off top of my head!" Ricky: "That's true, isn't it?"
ex: Have you seen the dregs they put on these shows? I mean people who couldn't get a job anywhere else!
What are you talking about? It's top caliber broadcasters on this station!
I can't name them off top of my head!
It's people who- They don't want on Radio 1 anymore.

q: Ricky wanted to film Karl's next trip home for TV. Which show did Steve point out was off air, before suggesting "The Pilkingtons"?
f: Ricky wanted to film it "for Channel 4 or something", and Steve reckoned "The Pilkingtons" would be "extraordinary".
ex: Can I- c- now I'm not being funny but next time you go home, can I film it?
Just for, do you know what I mean, Channel 4 or something?
Well, you know- I mean "The Osbournes" is not on at the moment--

q: Steve accidentally called stand-in presenter Claire Sturgess 'Karl'. After blaming the 'C' sound, what did he tell her?
